countries.name: イギリス

phrase.ja: ありがとう／乾杯（カジュアル）

countries.desc: ロンドンの街並みや、先史時代の遺跡ストーンヘンジがある国。英語が公用語なので、現地の英語にそのまま触れられます。

trips.name: ビッグ・ベン
trips.tip: 定番の撮影スポットはテムズ川の対岸やウェストミンスター橋の上。毎正時には鐘の音が聞こえます。
trips.desc: ロンドンのシンボル。国会議事堂の時計塔と大鐘。

article.title: Big Ben: The Voice of London
paragraphs: Big Ben is the nickname for the great bell inside the clock tower at the Palace of Westminster in London. Many people use the name for the whole tower, but its official name is the Elizabeth Tower.
The tower was completed in 1859. Its clock is known for being very accurate, and the bell's deep sound can be heard across central London.
After a long repair project, the tower reopened in 2022 with its clock faces painted in their original blue and gold colors.

questions.q: What is "Big Ben" originally the name of?
questions.hint: 第1段落の最初の文 “the nickname for …” に注目。
questions.explain: “Big Ben is the nickname for the great bell” とあり、もともとは大鐘の愛称です。

questions.q: What is the official name of the tower?
questions.hint: “official name” という語を探そう。
questions.explain: “its official name is the Elizabeth Tower” と書かれています。

questions.q: What happened in 2022?
questions.hint: 最後の段落の “reopened” の意味は？
questions.explain: 長い修復工事の後、2022年に再公開されました（reopened in 2022）。

summary.model: Big Ben is the great bell in the Elizabeth Tower in London. The tower was completed in 1859 and reopened in 2022 after repairs.

trips.name: ストーンヘンジ
trips.tip: ロンドンから日帰りツアーが多数出ている。平原は風が強いので上着があると安心。夏至の日の出の時期は特に人気。
trips.desc: 約5000年前に造られた巨石遺跡。謎の多い世界遺産。

article.title: The Mystery of Stonehenge
paragraphs: Stonehenge is a circle of huge standing stones on Salisbury Plain in southern England. It was built in several stages, starting about 5,000 years ago.
Some of the smaller stones came from Wales, more than 200 kilometers away. Nobody knows exactly how people moved them without modern machines.
The stones line up with the sun on the longest and shortest days of the year. Because of this, many people think Stonehenge was used as a calendar or a place for ceremonies.

questions.q: When did people start building Stonehenge?
questions.hint: 第1段落の “starting about …” を読もう。
questions.explain: “starting about 5,000 years ago” とあります。

questions.q: Where did some of the smaller stones come from?
questions.hint: “came from” の後ろに地名があります。
questions.explain: 小さめの石の一部は200km以上離れたウェールズから運ばれました。

questions.q: Why do people think it was used as a calendar?
choices: The stones line up with the sun
questions.hint: “Because of this” の “this” が指す内容は？
questions.explain: 石が夏至・冬至の太陽の向きと一直線に並ぶため、暦や儀式に使われたと考えられています。

summary.model: Stonehenge is a circle of huge stones built about 5,000 years ago. The stones line up with the sun, so it may have been a calendar.

trips.name: アフタヌーンティー
trips.tip: ホテルのアフタヌーンティーは人気なので予約がおすすめ。ドレスコードがある店もあるので事前に確認を。
trips.desc: 3段スタンドで楽しむ、イギリスのお茶の習慣。

article.title: Afternoon Tea: A Very British Habit
paragraphs: Afternoon tea is a famous British tradition. It is said that in the 1840s, Anna, the Duchess of Bedford, often felt hungry between lunch and a late dinner, so she started having tea and snacks in the afternoon.
Today, afternoon tea is usually served on a stand with three levels. Small sandwiches are on the bottom, scones with cream and jam are in the middle, and cakes are on the top.
People still argue about one question: should you put cream or jam on your scone first?

questions.q: Why did the Duchess start having afternoon tea?
choices: She was hungry between lunch and dinner
questions.hint: “so she started …” の前に理由があります。
questions.explain: 昼食と遅い夕食の間にお腹がすいたため、午後にお茶と軽食をとり始めました。

questions.q: What is in the middle of the stand?
questions.explain: 真ん中の段はクリームとジャムを添えたスコーンです。

questions.q: What do people still argue about?
choices: Whether to put cream or jam first
questions.hint: 最後の段落の “argue about” の後ろ。
questions.explain: スコーンにクリームとジャムのどちらを先に塗るか、今も議論になります。

summary.model: Afternoon tea is a British tradition started by a duchess who felt hungry in the afternoon. It is served on a three-level stand with sandwiches, scones, and cakes.

news.headline: Bike Commuting Doubles in Central London
news.script: Good evening. Cycling in central London has reached a record high. According to a new city report, the number of people riding bikes to work has doubled in the past five years. Officials say new bike lanes and lower traffic are the main reasons. Some drivers, however, complain that the roads have become too narrow. The city plans to add fifty more kilometers of bike lanes by next year.
news.summaryJa: ロンドン中心部で自転車通勤が過去5年で倍増。新しい自転車レーンと交通量の減少が主な理由。一方で道が狭くなったと不満を持つドライバーも。市は来年までにレーンを50km増やす予定。
news.summaryEn: Bike commuting in central London has doubled in five years thanks to new bike lanes and less traffic. The city will add 50 km more lanes next year.

questions.q: How much has bike commuting increased?
questions.explain: “has doubled in the past five years” = 過去5年で2倍になった。

questions.q: What do some drivers complain about?
questions.explain: “the roads have become too narrow” と不満を述べています。

questions.q: What does the city plan to do?
choices: Add fifty more kilometers of bike lanes
questions.hint: 最後の文 “The city plans to …”
questions.explain: 来年までに自転車レーンを50km追加する計画です。

countries.name: フランス
countries.desc: パリのエッフェル塔や、海に浮かぶ修道院モン・サン＝ミシェルがある国。カフェや食事も旅の楽しみのひとつです。

trips.name: エッフェル塔
trips.tip: チケットは公式サイトで事前予約がおすすめ。夜は毎正時に数分間きらめくライトアップを見逃さずに。
trips.desc: 1889年の万国博覧会のために建てられたパリの象徴。

article.title: The Eiffel Tower: From "Ugly" to Icon
paragraphs: The Eiffel Tower is the most famous symbol of Paris. It was built for the World's Fair in 1889 and designed by the company of engineer Gustave Eiffel. At first, many artists criticized the iron tower and called it ugly.
Today, about seven million people visit it every year. The tower is 330 meters tall, and visitors can take elevators or climb more than 600 steps to the second floor.
At night, the tower sparkles with thousands of lights for five minutes every hour.

questions.q: Why was the Eiffel Tower built?
choices: As a home for Gustave Eiffel
To watch ships on the river
As a radio station for the army
questions.hint: 第1段落の “built for …” に注目。
questions.explain: “It was built for the World's Fair in 1889” とあります。

questions.q: How did many artists feel about the tower at first?
choices: They did not know about it
questions.hint: “At first” から始まる文を読もう。
questions.explain: 当初、多くの芸術家が “ugly（醜い）” と批判しました。

questions.q: What happens at night?
choices: The tower changes color every day
questions.hint: 最後の段落 “sparkles” の意味は？
questions.explain: 夜は毎正時に5分間、数千の電球がきらめきます。

summary.model: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair. Once criticized, it is now the symbol of Paris and about seven million people visit it every year.

trips.name: モン・サン＝ミシェル
trips.tip: パリからの日帰りツアーも多いが、島内や対岸に泊まると夕景と夜景をゆっくり楽しめる。名物はふわふわのオムレツ。
trips.desc: 潮の満ち引きで姿を変える、海に浮かぶ修道院。

article.title: Mont-Saint-Michel: An Island of Tides
paragraphs: Mont-Saint-Michel is a small rocky island off the coast of Normandy in northern France. An abbey stands at the top, and a tiny village with narrow streets surrounds it.
The island is famous for its tides. When the tide is high, the sea surrounds the island, and when it is low, wide sands appear. In the past, pilgrims had to walk across the sand carefully.
Today, a bridge connects the island to the mainland, so visitors can reach it at any time.

questions.q: Where is Mont-Saint-Michel?
choices: On a mountain in the Alps
questions.hint: “off the coast of …” は「〜の沖に」。
questions.explain: フランス北部ノルマンディー地方の沖にある小さな岩の島です。

questions.q: What is the island famous for?
questions.explain: “The island is famous for its tides.” 潮の満ち引きで有名です。

questions.q: How do visitors reach the island today?
questions.explain: 今は橋が本土と島をつないでいて、いつでも行けます。

summary.model: Mont-Saint-Michel is a rocky island with an abbey in Normandy. It is famous for its tides, and today a bridge connects it to the mainland.

trips.name: パリのカフェ文化
trips.tip: カウンターで立って飲むとテーブル席より安いことが多い。店員さんには「Bonjour」とあいさつしてから注文するのがマナー。
trips.desc: 通りを眺めながら語らう、パリの日常の風景。

article.title: More Than Coffee: Café Life in Paris
paragraphs: In Paris, cafés are more than places to drink coffee. For hundreds of years, they have been places where people meet friends, read newspapers, and share ideas. Famous writers and artists once spent whole days at cafés such as the Café de Flore.
Many cafés have small tables on the sidewalk, called a terrace. People often sit side by side, facing the street, so they can watch people walk by.
If you order "un café," you will get a small, strong espresso, not a large cup of coffee.

questions.q: What have cafés been for hundreds of years?
choices: Places to meet, read, and share ideas
questions.explain: 友人と会い、新聞を読み、考えを語り合う場所でした。

questions.q: Why do people sit facing the street?
questions.hint: “so they can …” は「〜できるように」。
questions.explain: 通りを行き交う人を眺めるためです。

questions.q: What do you get if you order "un café"?
choices: A large cup of coffee with milk
questions.explain: “un café” を頼むと、小さくて濃いエスプレッソが出てきます。

summary.model: Paris cafés are places to meet people and share ideas. People sit on terraces facing the street, and "un café" means a small espresso.

news.headline: French Bakeries Struggle with Rising Butter Prices
news.script: French bakeries are facing a difficult year. The price of butter has risen by almost thirty percent, and many bakers say they cannot keep their croissants cheap. A baker in Lyon told reporters that she now pays twice as much as two years ago. Some shops have started making smaller croissants, while others have raised prices. Customers say they will still buy them, but less often.
news.summaryJa: フランスのパン屋がバター価格の高騰（約30％上昇）に苦しんでいる。リヨンのパン職人は2年前の2倍を払っていると話す。クロワッサンを小さくする店や値上げする店も。客は買う頻度を減らすと話している。
news.summaryEn: Butter prices in France have risen by almost 30 percent. Some bakeries are making smaller croissants or raising prices, and customers will buy them less often.

questions.q: How much has the price of butter risen?
questions.hint: “thirty” と “thirteen” の聞き分けに注意。
questions.explain: “risen by almost thirty percent” = 約30％上昇。

questions.q: Where is the baker who talked to reporters?
questions.hint: “A baker in …” の地名を聴こう。
questions.explain: “A baker in Lyon told reporters …” とあります。

questions.q: What have some shops started doing?
questions.explain: 一部の店はクロワッサンを小さくし始めました。

countries.name: イタリア
countries.desc: ローマのコロッセオや水の都ヴェネツィアなど、古代からの街並みが残る国。ナポリはピッツァ発祥の地として知られています。

trips.name: コロッセオ
trips.tip: 人気が高く当日券は並ぶことが多いので事前予約を。隣のフォロ・ロマーノも一緒に回るのがおすすめ。
trips.desc: 約5万人を収容した古代ローマ最大の円形闘技場。

article.title: Inside the Colosseum
paragraphs: The Colosseum in Rome is the largest amphitheater ever built in the Roman Empire. It was completed in the year 80 and could hold about 50,000 people.
Ancient Romans came here to watch gladiators fight and to see shows with wild animals. Under the floor, there were tunnels and rooms where animals and fighters waited.
Earthquakes and stone robbers damaged the building over the centuries, but it is still one of the most visited places in the world.

questions.q: About how many people could the Colosseum hold?
questions.explain: 約5万人（50,000）を収容できました。

questions.q: What was under the floor?
questions.explain: 床下には動物や剣闘士が待機するトンネルと部屋がありました。

questions.q: What damaged the building?
questions.explain: 地震と石泥棒によって何世紀もかけて損傷しました。

summary.model: The Colosseum in Rome could hold about 50,000 people who watched gladiators fight. It was damaged over time but is still very popular.

trips.name: ヴェネツィア
trips.tip: 移動は水上バス（ヴァポレット）が便利。混雑日は日帰り客に入場料がかかる場合があるので、旅行前に確認を。
trips.desc: 運河とゴンドラの水の都。高潮との戦いも。

article.title: Venice: A City on the Water
paragraphs: Venice is a city in northern Italy built on more than 100 small islands in a lagoon. Instead of roads, it has canals, and people travel by boat.
The most famous boats are gondolas, long black boats moved by a gondolier with a single oar. Today, most gondolas carry tourists rather than local people.
Venice faces a serious problem: flooding. During high tides, called "acqua alta," water covers the streets. The city built a system of moving barriers to protect itself from the sea.

questions.q: What does Venice have instead of roads?
questions.explain: 道路の代わりに運河（canals）があり、人々は船で移動します。

questions.q: Who mainly uses gondolas today?
questions.explain: 今日のゴンドラの多くは地元の人より観光客を乗せています。

questions.q: What is "acqua alta"?
choices: High tides that flood the streets
questions.explain: “acqua alta” は街に水があふれる高潮のことです。

summary.model: Venice is built on islands and has canals instead of roads. It suffers from flooding, so the city built moving barriers.

trips.name: ナポリのピッツァ
trips.tip: 人気店は行列ができることも多い。ピッツァは1人1枚が基本で、ナイフとフォークで食べてもOK。
trips.desc: ピザ発祥の地ナポリの、ユネスコ無形文化遺産の技。

article.title: Naples: The Home of Pizza
paragraphs: Naples, a city in southern Italy, is known as the home of pizza. A true Neapolitan pizza has a soft, thin center and a puffy edge called the "cornicione." It is baked in a very hot wood-fired oven for only about 60 to 90 seconds.
One of the most famous types is the Margherita. Its toppings, tomato, mozzarella, and basil, have the same colors as the Italian flag: red, white, and green.
In 2017, UNESCO added the art of Neapolitan pizza making to its list of Intangible Cultural Heritage.

questions.q: How long is a Neapolitan pizza baked?
questions.explain: とても熱い薪窯で、わずか60〜90秒ほどで焼き上げます。

questions.q: Why are the Margherita's toppings special?
choices: They match the colors of the Italian flag
questions.explain: トマト・モッツァレラ・バジルがイタリア国旗の赤・白・緑と同じ色です。

questions.q: What happened in 2017?
choices: The Margherita got a new name
questions.explain: ナポリのピッツァ職人の技がユネスコ無形文化遺産に登録されました。

summary.model: Naples is the home of pizza, which is baked quickly in a very hot oven. The Margherita has the colors of the Italian flag, and UNESCO recognized the art of making it.

news.headline: Rome Opens Ancient Sites for Night Tours
news.script: Rome is opening some of its ancient sites at night this summer. Visitors can now walk through parts of the Colosseum after dark with a guide. The tours start at eight in the evening and last about ninety minutes. Officials hope the night tours will reduce crowds during the hot afternoon. Tickets are limited, so travelers are advised to book online at least two weeks in advance.
news.summaryJa: ローマが夏の間、古代遺跡を夜間公開。コロッセオの一部をガイド付きで見学できる。ツアーは午後8時から約90分。暑い午後の混雑緩和が狙い。チケットは限定数のため2週間前までのオンライン予約が推奨されている。
news.summaryEn: Rome is offering guided night tours of the Colosseum this summer to reduce afternoon crowds. Tickets are limited, so book two weeks ahead.

questions.q: When do the night tours start?
questions.explain: ツアーは午後8時（eight p.m.）に始まります。

questions.q: Why are officials starting night tours?
choices: To reduce crowds in the hot afternoon
Because the site is closed during the day
questions.explain: 暑い午後の混雑を減らすためです。

questions.q: What are travelers advised to do?
choices: Book online at least two weeks in advance
questions.hint: “advised to …” は「〜するよう勧められる」。
questions.explain: 少なくとも2週間前にオンライン予約するよう勧められています。

countries.name: エジプト

phrase.ja: ありがとう（アラビア語）

countries.desc: ギザのピラミッドやナイル川沿いの神殿で知られる国。首都カイロでは、屋台料理のコシャリが定番です。

trips.name: ギザの大ピラミッド
trips.tip: 日差しが強いので帽子・水・日焼け止めは必須。朝早めの時間帯が比較的すいている。
trips.desc: 古代世界の七不思議で唯一現存する巨大建造物。

article.title: The Great Pyramid of Giza
paragraphs: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and the only one that still stands. It was built about 4,500 years ago as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu.
It is made of more than two million stone blocks. For almost 4,000 years, it was the tallest human-made structure on Earth.
Near the pyramids is the Great Sphinx, a giant statue with the body of a lion and the head of a human.

questions.q: Why was the Great Pyramid built?
choices: As a tomb for a pharaoh
questions.hint: “built … as a …” の “as” は「〜として」。
questions.explain: ファラオ（クフ王）の墓（tomb）として建てられました。

questions.q: How long was it the tallest human-made structure?
questions.explain: 約4000年もの間、人類が造った最も高い建造物でした。

questions.q: What does the Great Sphinx look like?
choices: A lion's head and a human body
A lion's body and a human head
questions.hint: “the body of …” と “the head of …” の順番に注意。
questions.explain: ライオンの体に人間の頭を持つ巨大な像です。

summary.model: The Great Pyramid was built about 4,500 years ago as a tomb for a pharaoh. It is the only Wonder of the Ancient World that still stands.

trips.name: アブ・シンベル神殿
trips.tip: アスワンから車や飛行機でアクセス。年に2回、朝日が神殿の奥まで差し込む日があり、多くの人が訪れる。
trips.desc: ダム建設から救うため丸ごと移設された岩窟神殿。

article.title: Abu Simbel: The Temple That Moved
paragraphs: Abu Simbel is a pair of huge rock temples in southern Egypt. They were carved into a mountain more than 3,000 years ago by order of the pharaoh Ramesses II.
Four giant statues of the king, each about 20 meters tall, sit at the entrance of the main temple.

In the 1960s, the temples were in danger because a new dam would flood the area. An international team cut the temples into large blocks and moved them to higher ground. It was one of the greatest rescue projects in history.

questions.q: Who ordered the temples to be built?
questions.explain: ファラオ、ラムセス2世の命令で造られました。

questions.q: What sits at the entrance of the main temple?
choices: Four giant statues of the king
questions.explain: 高さ約20mの王の巨像4体が入口に座っています。

questions.q: Why were the temples moved?
choices: A new dam would flood the area
questions.explain: 新しいダムで水没する恐れがあったため移設されました。

summary.model: Abu Simbel's temples were built by Ramesses II. In the 1960s they were cut into blocks and moved to save them from a new dam.

trips.name: コシャリ
trips.tip: コシャリ専門店は地元の人でにぎわう。量が多いので小さいサイズから試すのがおすすめ。辛いソースはお好みで。
trips.desc: 米・パスタ・豆を混ぜたエジプトの国民食。

article.title: Koshary: Egypt's Favorite Street Food
paragraphs: Koshary is one of Egypt's most popular street foods. It is a mix of rice, pasta, and lentils, topped with chickpeas, tomato sauce, and crispy fried onions.

Koshary is cheap, filling, and does not contain meat, so people of all ages and backgrounds enjoy it. In Cairo, there are restaurants that serve only koshary, and they are often full of local people at lunchtime.
Many people add a spicy sauce or a garlic and vinegar sauce to make the taste stronger.

questions.q: What is koshary mainly made of?
questions.explain: 米・パスタ・レンズ豆を混ぜた料理です。

questions.q: Why do people of all ages enjoy it?
choices: It is cheap, filling, and has no meat
It is only sold at night
questions.hint: “so people of all ages …” の前に理由。
questions.explain: 安くてお腹いっぱいになり、肉を使っていないため誰でも食べやすいからです。

questions.q: What do many people add to make the taste stronger?
choices: A spicy sauce or a garlic and vinegar sauce
questions.explain: 辛いソースや、にんにくと酢のソースを加えます。

summary.model: Koshary is a cheap and popular Egyptian street food made of rice, pasta, and lentils with tomato sauce and fried onions.

news.headline: New Museum Near the Pyramids Draws Crowds
news.script: A huge new museum near the pyramids of Giza is attracting visitors from around the world. Its most popular area shows thousands of treasures from the tomb of King Tutankhamun, displayed together for the first time. The museum also has a giant staircase lined with ancient statues. Tour companies say hotel bookings in Cairo have increased sharply since the opening.
news.summaryJa: ギザのピラミッド近くの巨大な新博物館に世界中から観光客が訪れている。一番人気はツタンカーメン王の墓の財宝数千点を初めてまとめて展示するエリア。古代の像が並ぶ大階段も。開館以来カイロのホテル予約が急増している。
news.summaryEn: A huge new museum near the pyramids shows Tutankhamun's treasures together for the first time. Hotel bookings in Cairo have risen sharply.

questions.q: Where is the new museum?
questions.explain: “near the pyramids of Giza” にあります。

questions.q: What is the most popular area?
questions.explain: ツタンカーメン王の墓の財宝の展示エリアです。

questions.q: What has increased since the opening?
questions.explain: カイロのホテル予約が急増しました。

countries.name: オーストラリア
countries.currency: オーストラリア・ドル

phrase.ja: やあ、こんにちは（オーストラリア英語）

countries.desc: シドニーのオペラハウスや、世界最大のサンゴ礁がある国。英語が主な言語で、独特の言い回しもあります。

trips.name: シドニー・オペラハウス
trips.tip: 建物の内部を見学できるガイドツアーがある。対岸からはハーバーブリッジと一緒に撮影できる。
trips.desc: 帆のような屋根が特徴の20世紀を代表する建築。

article.title: Sails on the Harbour
paragraphs: The Sydney Opera House is one of the most famous buildings of the 20th century. Its roof looks like white sails on Sydney Harbour.
The Danish architect Jørn Utzon won an international design competition in 1957. However, construction was difficult and expensive, and it took until 1973 to finish.
Today, the building hosts more than 1,500 performances a year, from opera and ballet to rock concerts. In 2007, it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q: What does the roof look like?
questions.hint: “looks like …” は「〜のように見える」。
questions.explain: 屋根は港に浮かぶ白い帆のように見えます。

questions.q: Where was the architect from?
questions.explain: “Danish” = デンマークの。建築家ウッツォンはデンマーク出身です。

questions.q: When did it become a World Heritage Site?
questions.explain: 2007年にユネスコ世界遺産に登録されました。

summary.model: The Sydney Opera House has a roof like white sails. It was finished in 1973, hosts many performances, and is a World Heritage Site.

trips.name: グレート・バリア・リーフ
trips.tip: ケアンズなどからボートツアーで行ける。サンゴを傷つけないよう、触らない・サンゴに優しい日焼け止めを使うのがマナー。
trips.desc: 宇宙からも見える世界最大のサンゴ礁。

article.title: The Great Barrier Reef in Danger
paragraphs: The Great Barrier Reef, off the coast of Queensland, is the largest coral reef system in the world. It is so big that it can be seen from space.
The reef is home to thousands of kinds of fish, as well as turtles, dolphins, and sharks. Coral is actually made of tiny living animals.
However, the reef is in danger. When the ocean becomes too warm, coral turns white and can die. This is called coral bleaching. Scientists and tourists are working together to protect it.

questions.q: What is special about the size of the reef?
choices: It can be seen from space
questions.hint: “so big that …” は「とても大きいので…」。
questions.explain: 宇宙からも見えるほど大きいサンゴ礁です。

questions.q: What is coral made of?
questions.explain: サンゴは実は小さな生き物（動物）でできています。

questions.q: What causes coral bleaching?
choices: Ocean water that is too warm
questions.explain: 海水温が高くなりすぎるとサンゴが白くなる（白化）。

summary.model: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef. Warm oceans cause coral bleaching, so people are working to protect it.

trips.name: ビーチ文化
trips.tip: 泳ぐときは必ず赤と黄色の旗の間で。日差しがとても強いので、日焼け止めとラッシュガードを忘れずに。
trips.desc: ボンダイビーチに見る、オーストラリアの海との暮らし。

article.title: Life at the Beach in Australia
paragraphs: For many Australians, the beach is a big part of everyday life. Bondi Beach in Sydney is one of the most famous, and people go there to swim, surf, or walk along the coast before work.
The ocean can be dangerous because of strong currents called rips. That is why volunteer lifesavers watch many beaches. Australia's first surf lifesaving clubs started in the early 1900s.
Visitors should always swim between the red and yellow flags. These flags show the safest area, where lifesavers are watching.

questions.q: What do people do at Bondi Beach before work?
questions.hint: 第1段落の “before work” を探そう。
questions.explain: 出勤前に泳いだり、サーフィンをしたり、海岸沿いを歩いたりします。

questions.q: What are "rips"?
questions.explain: rips は強い離岸流のことです。

questions.q: Where should visitors swim?
choices: Between the red and yellow flags
questions.explain: ライフセーバーが見ている、赤と黄色の旗の間で泳ぐのが決まりです。

summary.model: The beach is part of daily life in Australia. Because of dangerous rips, lifesavers watch the beaches, and visitors should swim between the red and yellow flags.

news.headline: Young Coral Recovering Faster Than Expected
news.script: Scientists in Queensland have shared some good news about the Great Barrier Reef. In several areas, young coral is growing faster than expected after last year's bleaching. Researchers say cooler water this season helped the coral recover. However, they warn that the reef is still at risk, and that reducing greenhouse gases is the only long-term solution.
news.summaryJa: グレート・バリア・リーフで、昨年の白化の後、若いサンゴが予想以上の速さで成長している。今季の海水温が低かったことが回復を助けた。ただし研究者は、サンゴ礁は依然危機にあり、温室効果ガスの削減が唯一の長期的解決策だと警告している。
news.summaryEn: Young coral on the Great Barrier Reef is recovering faster than expected thanks to cooler water, but scientists say cutting greenhouse gases is still necessary.

questions.q: What is growing faster than expected?
questions.explain: 若いサンゴ（young coral）が予想より速く成長しています。

questions.q: What helped the coral recover?
questions.explain: 今季の海水温が低かったことが回復を助けました。

questions.q: What is the only long-term solution?
questions.explain: 温室効果ガスを減らすことが唯一の長期的解決策です。

countries.desc: ニューヨークの自由の女神から西部のグランド・キャニオンまで、見どころが国中に点在しています。

trips.desc: フランスから贈られた自由と希望の象徴。

article.title: Lady Liberty: A Gift from France
paragraphs: The Statue of Liberty stands on Liberty Island in New York Harbor. It was a gift from the people of France to the United States and was dedicated in 1886.
The statue holds a torch in her right hand and a tablet in her left hand. The tablet shows the date of American independence, July 4, 1776.
For millions of immigrants arriving by ship, the statue was the first thing they saw of America. It became a symbol of freedom and hope.

questions.q: Who gave the statue to the United States?
questions.explain: フランスの人々からアメリカへの贈り物です。

questions.q: What does the tablet show?
questions.explain: 銘板にはアメリカ独立の日付（1776年7月4日）が刻まれています。

questions.q: What did the statue mean for immigrants?
choices: A symbol of freedom and hope
questions.hint: 最後の文 “It became a symbol of …”
questions.explain: 移民にとって自由と希望の象徴となりました。

summary.model: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France in 1886. For immigrants, it became a symbol of freedom and hope.

trips.name: グランド・キャニオン
trips.tip: 観光の中心は南側のサウスリム。標高が高く朝晩は冷えるので、夏でも羽織るものを持っていこう。
trips.desc: コロラド川が数百万年かけて刻んだ大峡谷。

article.title: Reading the Earth's History at the Grand Canyon
paragraphs: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is about 450 kilometers long and up to 1.8 kilometers deep. The Colorado River slowly carved it over millions of years.
The walls of the canyon show many layers of colorful rock. Each layer tells scientists about a different period in the Earth's history.
More than four million people visit the national park every year. Many enjoy watching the sunrise or sunset, when the rocks turn red, orange, and purple.

questions.q: What created the Grand Canyon?
questions.explain: コロラド川が数百万年かけて削り出しました。

questions.q: What do the rock layers tell scientists about?
choices: Only the age of the river
questions.explain: それぞれの地層が地球の歴史の異なる時代を教えてくれます。

questions.q: When do the rocks turn red, orange, and purple?
questions.explain: 日の出や日の入りの時に岩が赤やオレンジ、紫に染まります。

summary.model: The Grand Canyon was carved by the Colorado River. Its rock layers show the Earth's history, and millions of people visit it every year.

trips.name: 感謝祭
trips.tip: 11月第4木曜日の前後は帰省ラッシュで航空券が高くなりやすい。当日は休業するお店も多いので注意。
trips.desc: 家族で七面鳥を囲む、アメリカ最大級の祝日。

article.title: Thanksgiving: A Day for Family and Food
paragraphs: Thanksgiving is one of the biggest holidays in the United States. It is celebrated on the fourth Thursday of November, and many people travel long distances to be with their families.
The main dish is usually a roast turkey. It is served with mashed potatoes, stuffing, and cranberry sauce, and pumpkin pie is a popular dessert.
On Thanksgiving morning, millions of people watch a famous parade in New York with giant balloons. In the afternoon, many families watch American football on TV.

questions.q: When is Thanksgiving celebrated?
choices: On the fourth Thursday of November
On the first Monday of December
questions.explain: 11月の第4木曜日に祝われます。

questions.q: What is usually the main dish?
questions.explain: メインはローストした七面鳥です。

questions.q: What do many families watch in the afternoon?
questions.explain: 午後はテレビでアメリカンフットボールを見る家族が多いです。

summary.model: Thanksgiving is a big American holiday on the fourth Thursday of November. Families eat roast turkey together and watch a parade and football.

news.headline: National Parks Ask Visitors to Reserve Ahead
news.script: Several popular national parks in the United States, including the Grand Canyon area, are asking visitors to make reservations during the busy summer season. Park officials say the system will protect nature and reduce traffic jams at the entrance. Visitors without a reservation can still enter early in the morning or late in the evening. The rules will be reviewed at the end of the year.
news.summaryJa: グランド・キャニオン周辺を含むアメリカの人気国立公園が、夏の繁忙期に事前予約を求めている。自然保護と入口の渋滞緩和が目的。予約なしでも早朝や夕方以降は入園できる。ルールは年末に見直される予定。
news.summaryEn: Popular U.S. national parks now ask for reservations in summer to protect nature and reduce traffic. Visitors without one can enter early or late.

questions.q: When do visitors need reservations?
questions.explain: 夏の繁忙期に予約が必要です。

questions.q: Why are parks using the system?
choices: To protect nature and reduce traffic jams
questions.explain: 自然を守り、入口の渋滞を減らすためです。

questions.q: What can visitors without a reservation do?
choices: Enter early in the morning or late in the evening
questions.explain: 早朝または夕方以降なら入園できます。
